assessments.reasoning: The SPDX Data repository’s unsigned annotated object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets type commit, SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. That target is the revision serving the inspected detail.

The official detail gives licenseId etalab-2.0, name Etalab Open License 2.0 and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Its seeAlso and crossRef fields cite DISIC’s master LICENSE and LICENSE.pdf. The generated French text explicitly identifies version 2.0 and Etalab’s role.

The pinned first-party French Markdown establishes the publisher edition to which the crosswalk refers. Its authorship, title, version and substantive terms support that scope even though the SPDX reference points to a government copy.

The immutable DISIC LICENSE preserves the repository and file path of the SPDX raw master reference. Its dated heading, ministry example, IP wording and final Etalab attribution correspond to the generated French document. It supplies direct evidence of what that government copy contains at its pinned revision.

challenge.method: Checked the annotated tag target, case-sensitive detail ID, name, deprecation and both reference fields. Compared the actual SPDX licenseText, DISIC LICENSE and Etalab LO.md across the opening grant, attribution example, personal data, intellectual property, liability, applicable law, definitions and closing version statement. Tested a prior edition, a wrong author, branch drift and identical-text inference.
challenge.results: SPDX and DISIC both say Version 2.0, Avril 2017, use the ministry/data.gouv.fr example and qualify the IP transfer with “cessibles.” Etalab’s Markdown uses an INSEE/SIRENE example, phrases the IP provision differently and also mentions the heritage code. All three identify Etalab and the 2.0 edition, permit commercial and noncommercial reuse, require source and last-update attribution and select French law. Both SPDX crossRef entries record match as the string “false” alongside isValid and isLive set to true. Those historical fields provide no affirmative text-match result. The substantive comparison supports the narrower correspondence.

limitations: SPDX cites moving master routes for LICENSE and LICENSE.pdf. The fixed inspection covers the DISIC text at cf21e4cea2b28e259ba7503b5cdb9c614c6ccde3. The historical master tip at generation time, the PDF bytes and the English translation linked in the comment were not verified.

The three documents support edition-level correspondence. Differences in wording preclude a verbatim-equivalence finding. Legal equivalence, XML build lineage and grants for specific works remain unassessed.
reasoning: The generated SPDX detail identifies etalab-2.0 as Etalab Open License 2.0. Its cited DISIC text route has a commit-pinned counterpart whose document names Etalab, version 2.0 and April 2017. Independently comparing those documents with Etalab’s LO.md establishes the edition through authorship, grant, attribution condition, French-law clause and public-information purpose. SCES §§4 and 7 require challenging the cross-index relationship and accounting for derivative sources. The DISIC copy connects the reference to the named instrument without constituting independent authorship.
